claim.quote: Lower limits on the nucleon lifetime in channels containing at least one positron or muon are given. The analysis is based on 4 years of data taking with the Fréjus detector.

date.note: Publication month of Z. Phys. C 50, 385-394 (1991).

key_value_text.note: The Springer page text loses the superscripts and repeats a phrase ('1031' reads 10^31, '1.5·1032' reads 1.5x10^32); the modes are as printed in the abstract.
key_value_text.quote: The limits obtained range from 1031 years forp→e + K *0 to 1.5·1032 years forp→e + K *0 to 1.5·1032 years forp→µ + γ.
key_value_text.value: Lower limits on the nucleon lifetime from about 1e31 years (p to e+ K*0) up to 1.5e32 years (p to mu+ gamma), for channels with at least one positron or muon

name: Results from the Fréjus experiment on nucleon decay modes with charged leptons

summary.plain: Using four years of Fréjus data, no proton or neutron decay into a positron or muon was seen, so the experiment set lower limits on the lifetimes of nucleons for many decay channels, between about 10^31 and 1.5 x 10^32 years.
summary.technical: No signal in channels containing at least one positron or muon; lower nucleon-lifetime limits of about 1e31 yr (p to e+ K*0) to 1.5e32 yr (p to mu+ gamma), with the atmospheric-neutrino background estimated in several ways and two nuclear models used for the event simulation.

title: Results from the Fréjus experiment on nucleon decay modes with charged leptons
why_it_matters: One of the first-generation proton-decay searches that ruled out the simplest grand unified models alongside IMB and Kamiokande; no experiment has seen nucleon decay.
